summary:
ASTROVITAL is a web-based astronaut health intelligence and early-warning demonstration platform developed using Python and Streamlit.

It allows users to enter health indicators such as heart rate, SpO₂, body temperature, sleep duration, stress, and fatigue. The system analyses these inputs using illustrative rule-based logic and displays health status, alerts, recommendations, and simulated health trends through an interactive dashboard.

The project addresses the challenge of astronaut health monitoring by demonstrating how multiple health indicators can be combined in one platform to highlight values that may need attention. It also references NASA's OSD-574 Inspiration4 skin microbiome study to connect the project with real space biology research.

Astronaut health is essential for crew safety and mission success. ASTROVITAL demonstrates how accessible digital tools and explainable alerts could support health awareness during space missions.

Note: This is an educational prototype. Health readings and historical trends are simulated, thresholds are illustrative, and the platform is not clinically validated or intended for medical diagnosis.
details:
ASTROVITAL

Tagline: Your Health. Our Mission. Smarter Space Exploration.

Short Description

ASTROVITAL is an astronaut health monitoring and early-warning prototype designed to help visualize health indicators, identify potential concerns through explainable rules, and support astronaut health awareness during space missions.

Project Description

Astronauts experience challenging conditions during space missions, including microgravity, disrupted sleep cycles, stress, and changes in their physical environment. Continuous awareness of health indicators is important for supporting astronaut safety and mission performance.

ASTROVITAL is a web-based health intelligence dashboard developed using Python and Streamlit. It allows users to enter astronaut health parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, sleep duration, stress, and fatigue.

The system uses a rule-based health assessment engine to identify readings that fall outside illustrative demonstration thresholds. It displays risk categories, alerts, recommendations, health indicators, and simulated historical trends.

The platform also includes a NASA space-health research section referencing the Inspiration4 microbiome study (OSD-574), connecting the prototype with real space-health research.

ASTROVITAL aims to demonstrate how accessible data visualization and explainable health-monitoring logic can support future astronaut health-monitoring systems.

Key Features

  • Astronaut health monitoring dashboard.
  • Heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, sleep, stress, and fatigue inputs.
  • Rule-based early-warning alerts.
  • Health risk categorization and recommendations.
  • Simulated health trend visualizations.
  • Downloadable health assessment report.
  • NASA OSD-574 research information and source links.

Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Streamlit
  • Programming Language: Python
  • Data Handling: Pandas
  • Backend: Python health assessment engine
  • Visualization: Streamlit charts
  • Version Control: Git and GitHub

NASA Data and Research

NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), including the OSD-574 Inspiration4 skin microbiome study, is referenced in the research section. The current prototype does not independently process the original sequencing files or use them to calculate live astronaut vital signs.

Expected Impact

ASTROVITAL demonstrates an accessible and explainable approach to astronaut health awareness. It can serve as a foundation for future systems incorporating validated medical thresholds, real wearable-device data, and more advanced predictive analytics.

Limitations

This is an educational prototype, not a medical device or clinically validated diagnostic system. Demonstration health inputs and illustrative thresholds are used; simulated charts do not represent actual astronaut measurements.
